articles.title: Golden State Valkyries win first WNBA championship
articles.summary: Gabby Williams scored her team's final 11 points of the third quarter and dazzled through the fourth on the way to 30 points as the Golden State Valkyries captured the WNBA championship in just their second season.
body: The Valkyries beat the Atlanta Dream 68-63 to claim a sensational first WNBA Finals Game 7 on Saturday night as Williams scored 28 of her 30 points in the final 20 minutes.

The 30-year-old star won a championship in college, but had fallen just short while playing for France in the Olympics and FIBA World Cup, losing to the US for the gold medal at the 2024 Paris Games by a point and in the women's FIBA World Cup this September.
Now in her first chance on the WNBA's biggest stage, Williams wouldn't let the opportunity slip away.
"I just walked into a group full of love," Williams said. "And that just changed the entire trajectory of my career."

articles.title: Michael Carrick to stay in charge of Manchester United for Roma game
articles.summary: United 17th in Premier League after Chelsea defeat. No change expected until international break. Michael Carrick is set to remain in charge of Manchester United for Tuesday’s Champions League game against Roma at Old Trafford despite Saturday’s 2-0 loss at Chelsea.
body: The defeat means United have not won in nine games and have made their poorest start to a season since 1988, but Carrick’s position is expected to be reviewed again during the the next international break after the next round of Premier League matches, United hosting Aston Villa on Sunday.

The 45-year-old came close to losing his job last Monday when Jason Wilcox, and Omar Berrada, met at the training ground to discuss his future. The director of football and the chief executive decided Carrick should be given a chance to turn form and results around.
Carrick’s side are in 17th with seven points, above the relegation only on goal difference.
There remains a view within the hierarchy that Carrick can still transform fortunes, with United’s travelling support still backing him at the end of the defeat at Stamford Bridge on Saturday.

articles.title: Rampant Salford hint that Beckham’s lofty ambitions are not a pipe dream
articles.summary: The aim of reaching the Championship looks more realistic for a Manchester club in the shadow of City and United. After seven seasons in League Two, Salford City are finally threatening to match the hype brought by their high-profile owners.
body: The budget has increased, allowing the club to sign a number of players who will feel they are above League Two standard. Striker Macaulay Langstaff arrived from Millwall; the last time he played at this level, he scored 28 goals in a season for Notts County. Matchwinner Will Aimson spent the past two seasons in the division above with Wigan and has dropped down because of Salford’s project.

In terms of personnel, the most notable change was in the dugout where 48-year-old Peter Cklamovski replaced Karl Robinson, who was sacked after a desperate performance in the playoff final loss to Notts County. His previous experience came working under Ange Postecoglou before becoming a head coach in his own right in Asia, most recently taking charge of the Malaysia national team. Such was his unknown status, Salford’s chief football adviser Paul Scholes had to Google the Australian before he was appointed.

articles.title: 'An inspiration to so many' - Olympic runner Mageean dies aged 34
articles.summary: Portaferry runner Ciara Mageean, who won a European title and twice represented Ireland at the Olympics, dies aged 34.
body: European champion and two-time Olympian Ciara Mageean has died at the age of 34.
Mageean represented Ireland at the 2016 and 2020 Olympics, but was forced to withdraw from the 2024 Paris Games because of an Achilles injury.
Earlier in 2024, she had clinched the first major title of her career when she took 1500m gold at the European Championships in Rome.
Prior to that she had also represented Northern Ireland at the Commonwealth Games, winning 1500m silver at Birmingham 2022.

articles.summary: Kilmarnock climb out of bottom spot, but failure to beat 10 men at home adds to gloom at Rugby Park.
body: Four goals shared, some excellent football played, and a plethora of chances created by the home side. All greeted on the final whistle by a loud, piercing chorus of boos and some angry finger-pointing by sections of the Kilmarnock support.
That such fan fury follows a result that actually moved the Ayrshire side off the bottom of the Scottish Premiership tells its own story.
The patience of the Rugby Park regulars appears to be wearing thin. A worry for under-pressure manager Neil McCann, whose side have only enjoyed two league wins all season.

To fail to beat St Johnstone at home when the visitors played for 80 minutes with 10 men would be a difficult one for any manager to swallow, never mind one for whom every win must feel like a life jacket in stormy sea.

articles.title: Yamashita holds off Liu to defend her LPGA Maybank Championship title
articles.summary: Miyu Yamashita successfully defended her title at the LPGA Tour's Maybank Championship on Sunday, beating China's Yan Liu by two strokes.
body: The 2025 Women's Open winner and third-round leader ended with a 72-hole total of 22-under after a final-round 68 on the Kuala Lumpur Golf and Country Club course.
The Japanese golfer sank five birdies with just the one bogey at the par-4 ninth in a near-perfect week where she led from Friday's second round until the final hole.

It was the 25-year-old's fifth career title and second in the LPGA Tour this season after she took a wire-to-wire, nine-stroke victory in the CPKC Women's Open at Royal Mayfair in Edmonton, Alberta in August.

"Yan Liu hits the ball with so much power and distance. She was making birdies early and hitting aggressive shots. I felt like I couldn't let my guard down for a single moment until the final putt dropped on the 18th."

articles.title: “Every Time When Adversity Hits, He’s Lost”: CFB Fans Rip Ryan Day As Ohio State Loses 30–18 to Lincoln Riley’s USC
articles.summary: Ryan Day’s Ohio State Buckeyes suffered a disappointing 30-18 defeat to Lincoln Riley’s USC Trojans. Day’s offensive approach came under scrutiny as the Buckeyes repeatedly stalled in the red zone and settled for field goals instead of touchdowns.
body: The absence of starting quarterback Julian Sayin certainly made things more difficult, but Day is still being criticized for his team’s lack of execution. Ohio State looked out of rhythm for much of the night, and the late touchdown did little to change the outcome.

For a team that entered the season with national championship ambitions, losing to USC is a significant setback. Day now faces pressure to get the Buckeyes back on track before their playoff hopes take another hit.
“Ryan Day would be an amazing GM but he’s not a good coach. Everytime when adversity hits hes lost. A coach has to be able to adapt and he can’t,” a fan wrote.
“I just can’t support Ryan Day like y’all do he’s an average coach living off the brand name. If he were a serious coach he’d have 3 Natties and I’m dead serious,” a fan wrote.

articles.title: 'Should retire': Bhuvneshwar Kumar brutally trolled by fans as India pacer ends comeback NZ series on disappointing note
articles.summary: Bhuvneshwar Kumar faced harsh fan trolling on social media as his India T20I comeback series against New Zealand ended with disappointing figures.
body: 'Should retire': Bhuvneshwar Kumar brutally trolled by fans as India pacer ends comeback NZ series on disappointing note originally appeared on Cricket News. Add Cricket News as a Preferred Source by clicking here.

Disgruntled fans have asked Bhuvneshwar Kumar to retire, and the criticism on social media is a sign of how quickly the mood has turned against the India pacer after his comeback series against New Zealand ended on a flat note in Hamilton, where he conceded 31 runs in his first three overs of the fifth T20I.

His return to the national T20I side was widely welcomed when it was announced. He was 36 and had spent four years out of the setup, so the cricket community saluted his grit and determination, and many believed he could solve some of India’s bowling worries.

Those hopes were never quite met in the first three matches, because he returned figures of 0/49, 1/50 and 0/40. The team management then dropped him for the fourth game in Auckland, which India lost by a heavy margin of 87 runs.
